description: PIC X(n) is space-padded on the RIGHT - the alphanumeric half of the fill contract in AAP section 0.3.7, and the complement of the PIC 9(n) zero-fill that cases 08, 09 and 10 pin. Two clean records are seeded, chosen because they carry the longest name values the whole fixture holds and therefore make the padding widest where it is still reviewable by hand: app/data/ASCII/custdata.txt line 11, CUST-ID 000000011, whose CUST-LAST-NAME at 60-84 is Pfannerstill - 12 characters of a 25-byte span, leaving 13 trailing spaces, the longest last name in the dataset ahead of Schowalter at 10 and Ankunding at 9 - and line 47, CUST-ID 000000047, whose CUST-FIRST-NAME at 10-34 is Rigoberto - 9 characters of 25, leaving 16 trailing spaces, the longest first name ahead of Immanuel at 8. Those two counts are computed from the widths app/cpy/CVCUS01Y.cpy declares rather than estimated (practice B11): 25 minus 12 is 13, and 25 minus 9 is 16. Not one name field in any of the fifty rows uses all 25 of its bytes, so trailing-space fidelity is not an edge condition in this dataset, it is the normal condition: the three 25-byte name spans, the three 50-byte address lines and the two 15-byte phone spans are mostly trailing spaces on both rows, and every one of those spaces is significant payload rather than trimmable whitespace. Row 11 leaves 19, 19 and 13 bytes of its three name spans unused and 29, 42 and 37 of its three address lines; row 47 leaves 16, 18 and 19 and then 30, 42 and 33; each phone span carries 13 characters and two trailing spaces on both rows. The case catches the two failure modes a PIC X codec has, and it distinguishes them. A codec that trims a field on read and does not re-pad it on write emits a short field, which shifts every span after it and makes the record 499 or fewer characters - caught by the total width, which FieldDiffer checks before it compares a single field. A codec that pads on the wrong side puts Rigoberto 16 bytes into its span instead of at the front: the record is still exactly 500 characters and every character of the value is still present, so only a comparison at the declared offset of CUST-FIRST-NAME detects it, which is precisely why FieldDiffer compares field by field rather than as whole strings. Both rows are therefore pinned twice over on the final-state channel - once span by span across all 19 names, so a difference is reported against the field that holds it, and once as the complete 500-character image, so the total width and the presence of every span are proved independently of the names. The neighbouring spans show the two fill rules side by side, and the fixture makes the contrast sharper than the copybook alone would: CUST-ADDR-ZIP is PIC X(10) at 240-249 and holds 24984 followed by five spaces on row 11, while on row 47 the same span is full - 31329-6973, a hyphenated ZIP+4 whose hyphen is exactly why the span is alphanumeric and not numeric - whereas CUST-SSN is PIC 9(09) at 280-288 and is zero-filled with no space anywhere in it, 493538586 on row 11 and 029222192 on row 47, where that leading zero is significant and is never normalised away. Two digit-bearing spans, 40 bytes apart, governed by opposite fill rules. The trailing FILLER PIC X(168) at 333-500 is blank on both rows, so both record lines end in a space and both are exactly 500 characters (gates G19 and G21); FILLER is named in the field map like any other span, because a byte no expectation covers is a byte that can be wrong while the diff count is zero. The run is clean, so app/cbl/CBCUS01C.cbl displays each record twice and emits 1 + (2 x 2) + 1 = 6 lines: the L71 banner, then for each record the raw group image from the 00 arm of 1000-CUSTFILE-GET-NEXT at L96 immediately followed by the mainline DISPLAY CUSTOMER-RECORD at L78, which is the same area with no statement between the two that could change it, and then the L85 banner. The duplication is a preserved defect and stays duplicated (practice B5); de-duplicating it would halve every fingerprint this program produces. The third READ reports 10, takes the L98 end-of-file arm, moves Y into END-OF-FILE and so suppresses the L78 display, contributing no line at all; the OPEN at L120 and the CLOSE at L138 both report 00 and emit nothing (gate G47). RETURN-CODE is never referenced in the 178 lines of the program, so GOBACK at L87 returns 0, and the CALL CEE3ABD site at L158 is out of reach - gate G35 is deliberately not exercised here. CUST-PRI-CARD-HOLDER-IND PIC X(01) at 329 is Y on both rows because it is Y on all fifty rows of the fixture and no N exists anywhere in it; none is invented (practice B5). Lines 11 and 47 are not contiguous, so they are declared inline rather than as a fixture slice, which can only narrow to a contiguous run; every byte of both is copied verbatim out of the real app/data/ASCII/custdata.txt (gate G16) and none is synthesized, and because that fixture matches its copybook width exactly no normalisation is declared. The bytes are US-ASCII, stated rather than assumed (practice B8). The dataset is addressed by the binding key CUSTFILE alone - the name the SELECT at app/cbl/CBCUS01C.cbl:L29 assigns it and the name the single DD of app/jcl/READCUST.jcl STEP05 mounts - so no dataset name reaches the case (gate G46), and because that step is a bare EXEC PGM= with no PARM the job parameters are empty. expectedWrites is empty as the positive assertion that the program issues no WRITE, no REWRITE and no DELETE, and the dataset-level expectation states the count and the width together - two rows of 500 bytes on the FINAL_STATE channel - because a row-level expectation alone cannot assert a width. Per requirement I1 the date-of-birth span is the hyphenated CUST-DOB-YYYY-MM-DD that app/cpy/CVCUS01Y.cpy declares at 309-318, and it is the only spelling this case may name; the differently spelled date-of-birth item at the same offset in app/cpy/CUSTREC.cpy belongs to a separate copybook that the statement programs model as their own type, and the two are never conflated. R1 caveat: CustomerFileReaderJob is a Spring Batch job by mandated name only and CustomerRepository is a repository by mandated name only - the source Function header reads Read and print customer data file, the program computes nothing and it writes no dataset. Baseline provenance (practice B12): these expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED from the control flow of app/cbl/CBCUS01C.cbl, the byte layout app/cpy/CVCUS01Y.cpy declares, the step and DD contract of app/jcl/READCUST.jcl and the real 50-row app/data/ASCII/custdata.txt fixture. They were NEVER captured from, recorded against or replayed from a live COBOL execution: running the legacy programs is empirically impossible in this environment, as AAP section 0.7.6 establishes with eight independently verified blockers, and the substitution of provenance is escalated as risk R-A rather than absorbed silently. Gates discharged: G15 (the twentieth and final case this program owns, completing the required twenty), G16 (seeded from the real fixture), G18 (the diff count must be zero across all twenty before the module is complete), G19 (both record lines exactly 500 characters, the width CVCUS01Y declares), G21 (FILLER X(168) at 333-500 present and space-filled on both lines), G47 (the 00 open, two 00 reads, the 10 end-of-file and the 00 close) and G51 (the unit is CustomerFileReaderJob driven at tasklet level with CustomerService as the decision-holding collaborator, no JobLauncher and no HTTP layer in the path).
